messages:
alex: ran a couple of microbenchmarks on the MoE routing path after yesterday's kernel change — seeing 95th tail latency spikes on generation when expert sparsity > 0.12. flamegraph attached: https://perf/reports/moe-routing-176960

alex: the weird bit is all-reduce time jumps by ~8-12ms for small tensors (<= 64KB) during token redistribution. overall throughput fine, but tails tank for some requests.

jin: curious — are these tiny tensors coming from per-expert KV slices?

alex: yeah, per-expert activation fragments + KV cache lookups produce lots of small messages during the routing phase. payload sizes very skewed.

elaine: did the kernel tweak change reduce kernel fusion or alter NCCL launch shapes?

alex: the new kernel picks different matmul tiling for int8 path which reduced single-GPU latency, but it changed timing so routing all-to-alls no longer overlap well with compute. perf trace here: `perf trace --timeline moe_routing.json` (see link above).

sam: can you paste the perf counters output? even approximate sizes help.

alex: sure, snippet from the run: 
```
# sample
timestamp, tensor_bytes, nccl_time_ms, compute_ms
1769601235, 48k, 11.9, 2.8
1769601236, 32k, 10.7, 1.9
1769601240, 320k, 2.3, 6.1
```
small ones dominate the gauge.

jin: small messages -> NCCL overhead. If we can aggregate per-device messages into fewer larger messages before all-to-all we should drop nccl latency significantly. batching window?

elaine: what about increasing KV cache page size or coalescing adjacent expert slices into a single transfer at the router? Might need allocator changes.

sam: or hierarchical routing: do local all-to-all across pipeline/tensor peers first, then global. reduces cross-node small-message count.

alex: tried simple coalescing at router level (10ms batching window) — reduced 95th by ~7ms but increased median by 0.8ms. tradeoff looks promising for tail-sensitive endpoints.

jin: can we do adaptive window: only coalesce when queue depth < X and request SLA allows? so high-priority requests bypass.

elaine: also investigate overlapping: move routing comms earlier and prefetch KV pages while compute finishing. right now kernel reorder removed a small depend that used to give overlap.

alex: good point — the kernel selection changes removed the implicit slack that enabled comm/compute overlap. we can modify scheduling to reintroduce overlap without reverting kernel.

sam: another leaky bucket: token routing fanout when many tokens target same expert creates congestion hot spots. applying local per-expert token caps (throttle to 16 tokens/expert per step) seems to smooth traffic. tests?

alex: ran token cap experiment: capped at 16/expert per step -> all-reduce time distribution tighter, overall throughput dropped 4% but 99th improved 18%. attaching raw csv: https://perf/reports/moe-tokencap-176960

jin: that's a good trade for customer-facing SLOs. we should surface this as a runtime policy (configurable per-deployment).

elaine: include a metric and alert for small-message ratio (bytes < 64k / total comm ops). if it rises above 0.3 trigger adaptive-coalesce.

perf-bot: automated report generated: moe-routing-regression-176960 — root cause candidate: kernel tiling change -> reduced comm/compute overlap; mitigation: router coalescing + per-expert throttling.

alex: action items: 1) jin -> prototype adaptive coalescer (PR target EOW), 2) elaine -> scheduler tweak to reintroduce overlap (investigate prefetch ordering), 3) sam -> perf tests for hierarchical all-to-all (POC). I'll paste test harness and baseline numbers in the thread.

jin: noted, will include opt-out flag for latency-sensitive routes.

elaine: also add a synthetic that simulates hot expert skew (zipf alpha tunable) so we can benchmark effectively.

sam: i'll spin load driver and run across cluster C tomorrow morning.

alex: thanks team. we should aim to ship router coalescer behind a flag and run canary on dedicated pool. will update the ticket with links. :thumbsup:
